Riya Nair: Quick idea dump: separate the "retire" lifetime from free/reuse to avoid allocator-runner races during page moves. Seen repro where runner frees a page, allocator immediately reuses it, and a late DMA completion stomps new content.
Laura Chen: Oof. We saw that in perf tests. How would retire semantics look?
Riya Nair: Proposal: when a page is migrated, we atomically publish the new location with a sequence/version number, mark the old page RETIRING with a retire_epoch = current_epoch + retire_epochs, and only reclaim after that epoch. Retire_epochs default=1. This gives a deterministic window for in-flight completions.
Mike K: That sounds similar to RCU-ish grace periods. Any perf impact for memory pressure?
Riya Nair: Small. We bound the extra resident pages by tunables and by preferring in-place coalesces first. Also add a fast-path: if migration is local and copy completes synchronously (no DMA), we can fast-commit without retiring.
Sara Patel: How do consumers find the live page? Do we need indirection table lookups on every access?
Riya Nair: Use a two-word header: {ptr, seq}. Readers do an atomic read of both; if seq is odd (migrating) they spin/try again or follow a helper. Checkout pseudocode:
```
read_page(addr):
  while True:
    (p, s) = atomic_read_header(addr)
    data = access(p)
    (p2, s2) = atomic_read_header(addr)
    if p==p2 and s==s2 and s%2==0:
      return data
    pause()
```
The seq toggles to an odd value while migrating. No global quiesce.
Dan O'Neill: Nice. What about cross-node moves where cost is high (PCIe/NVMe)? We need a move-cost estimator to avoid thrashing.
Riya Nair: Agreed. Add a lightweight cost model: cost_move = bytes*bandwidth_weight + pages*cpu_weight + pcie_latency. Expected benefit = estimated reduced page-faults * token_latency_saving. Move only if benefit*profit_factor > cost_move. Keep model linear and calibrate with telemetry.
Mike K: How to estimate reduced page-faults? Cheap heuristic: use sampled hotness + eviction history. If a page has been faulted N times in last T, assign benefit=N*avg_fault_cost.
Sara Patel: For hotness, we should reuse the 1% sampled EMA approach. Also expose per-tenant "defrag_aggressiveness" to respect SLOs. Tenants with strict SLO get defrag_aggressiveness=0.
Laura Chen: Rollout plan thoughts?
Riya Nair: Phase 0: unit tests + microbench of retire list correctness. Phase 1: lab canary with retire_epochs=2 and compact_budget small. Phase 2: measurement on embedding workloads, watch p99 token latency, tail DMA completion counters, and retired-resident ratio.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster "defrag-probe-2" scheduled for branch "retire-list-migration" :eyes:
Dan O'Neill: Metrics to add: retired_pages_count, retire_epoch_wait_ms, move_cost_estimate_hist, stale-write-detects. We'll want alerts if retired-resident_ratio > 0.2 under normal load.
Mike K: Edge: memory pressure spike could force us to drop retire semantics and reclaim early. We need a safe abort: mark page ABORT_RECLAIM and coordinate with allocator to prefer zeroing before reuse.
Riya Nair: Right, add a forced_reclaim path that only returns pages to the allocator after an atomic fence and zeroing step; also increment a metric reclaimed_under_pressure_count.
Sara Patel: I'll prototype the sampled hotness + eviction signal hook. Laura, want me to pair on the indirection header atomic semantics?
Laura Chen: Yup, I can help. Riya, can you sketch the on-disk/telemetry labels so we can later study cost_model calibration?
Riya Nair: Will do. Sketch for config snippet:
```
retire_config {
  retire_epochs: 1
  max_retired_ratio: 0.15
  force_reclaim_threshold: 0.9
  move_profit_factor: 1.2
}
```
Riya Nair: I'll open a WIP PR with tests + simple perf harness. Volunteers to review?
Mike K: I'll review the atomic header code.
Sara Patel: I'll review sampling + metrics.
Dan O'Neill: I'll run the canary perf and sanity checks.
Riya Nair: Thanks. Goal: eliminate late-DMA stomps and make compaction safe without global pauses. Short note will follow in the repo with diagrams. :thumbsup:
